While the story is exceptionally well-written and emotionally believable, its strength comes from psychological insight, witty metaphors, and character dynamics rather than sensory details. The narrator describes the events almost entirely through abstract reflection and intellectual observation. Although objects and foods are mentioned (such as "good olive oil," "pasta," "tea," "broth," and "clay figures"), they are used as narrative props or symbols of character traits rather than sensory experiences. The writer never actually describes how the food tastes or smells, what the house on Prospect Street looks like visually (colors, shapes, lighting), the textures of the objects, or the ambient sounds and temperatures of the environment.
